thread:
incident-bot: PAGED: p99 streaming latency spike detected in prod (region: eu-west-1). Alerts: p99 > 3s for SSE route /v1/generate/stream. Auto-escalation: page oncall.

oncall-amber: I'm on it. seeing a big tail on chunk arrival times, many connections stuck in 'WAITING' state at the proxy. p95 also degraded. Starting triage.

sre-noah: grabbing traces. traffic shows a cohort of long-lived websocket/SSE clients with very small ACK windows, looks like slow consumers/backpressure. Proxy write buffer is backing up, hitting TIME_WAIT spikes and then 504s from upstream.

eng-runtime: any deploys recently to streaming proxy or the runtime? I don't see infra changes in the last 6h. Model autoscales were normal.

support-jin: multiple customers reported intermittent partial responses and stalled streams in last 20m. One customer (org: MeldCorp) says their UI hangs when live streaming. Logging their ticket.

oncall-amber: mitigation idea: enable adaptive-client-throttle on the proxy (drops silent consumers after 30s of no read) and flip streaming-fallback-to-polling for affected route to reduce pressure while we investigate.

ops-elaine: rolling a proxy config change to eu-west-1 edge pool with conservative rollout. patch: `proxy.config.write_timeout_ms = 45000` and `proxy.features.adaptive_throttle = true` — applying canary to 2 nodes now.

Deploy-bot: rolling config change started. Canary nodes: proxy-eu-02, proxy-eu-04.

sre-noah: attaching a quick diagnostic:```
Top blocked connections (eu-west-1):
- proxy-eu-02: 124 stuck writes, avg blocked 22s
- proxy-eu-04: 137 stuck writes, avg blocked 19s
Upstream queue depth: model-pool-1: 48
```

eng-runtime: is KV cache or prefix caching causing backpressure on runtime? If clients are re-requesting prefixes, runtime could be saturating output buffers.

sre-noah: traces show the runtime responding but the proxy cannot flush to clients because of slow TCP window. So runtime isn't blocked, proxy queues grow and proxy starts timing out upstream requests causing 504s and increased p99.

pm-aly: customer impact assessment: estimated affected sessions ~2.3k in eu-west, error budget burn p99: 9x usual for streaming routes. Priority: high due to core streaming SLA.

support-jin: creating incident post to notify impacted customers with suggested workaround: use non-streaming generate endpoint (polling) or reduce parallel connections per client.

oncall-amber: Canary looks good for first 6m — stuck connections on canary nodes dropped by ~80%, p99 started to recover slightly. Proceeding to roll to remaining edge nodes.

Deploy-bot: config rollout to remaining edge nodes started.

eng-runtime: long term fix suggestions: implement per-connection backpressure metrics, make proxy honor per-client max inflight-chunks and expose signals to autoscaler. Also consider increasing proxy keepalive and tuning Nagle/linger.

ops-elaine: full rollout done at +14m. Monitoring shows p99 back to baseline after 3m post-rollout. We'll keep throttle active for 24h and revert to default after stability window.

sre-noah: follow-up items noted: 1) add synthetic slow-consumer tests, 2) alert on proxy blocked-write-count > 50 for >5m, 3) add dashboard for streaming queue depth.

pm-aly: schedule a postmortem with SRE + Runtime + Proxy owners tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Also send customers a summary and ETA for permanent mitigations.

support-jin: customer notification: "We deployed protective throttles to mitigate streaming stalls in EU. If you still see issues, please reply to ticket #INC-8342 and include a sample session id."

oncall-amber: handing off to SRE for post-incident follow-up. tagging @sre-noah for action items. Thanks everyone.

sre-noah: taking handoff. I'll coordinate the postmortem and own the follow-up tasks. Adding action items to the incident board.

incident-bot: Incident resolved. duration: 27m. severity: Sev2. Links: monitoring, traces, runbook.
